text: {"final": {"findings": [{"id": "R6", "statement": "Corrected: there is no send_sms(phone, text) function and messages are never free text. The only sending path is queue_sms(household_id: str, template_id: str, params: dict, *, now=None) -> SmsMessage, which requires template_id to be a key in TEMPLATES (REGISTERED, DELIVERY_DAY, DELIVERY_MOVED, PAYMENT_SENT, REVIEW, PRIORITY) and raises KeyError otherwise. The filled-in text is limited to MAX_LENGTH = 140 characters, enforced in render(template_id, params) which raises ValueError if len(text) > 140. queue_sms also requires feature('sms_enabled') to be true, requires the household to have sms_ok set (else ValueError), looks up the phone via get_household(household_id), assigns a new ID via format_sms_id(next_number(..., 'SMS-')), and appends the SmsMessage dict (fields: id, household_id, phone, template_id, params, text, queued_at) to outbox/sms.jsonl. The outbox is irreversible: nothing removes or edits a line. Gateway delivery results are in data/sms_status.json as {\"SMS-00001\": \"delivered\", \"SMS-00002\": \"failed\", ...}, readable via delivery_status(); new messages have no entry yet. To resend a failed message, re-queue with the original message's template_id and params (from sent_messages()), not its text.", "file": "notifications/sms.py"}]}}
